lede: Today's search produced 5 strong originals inside 1 day. The final set is the top 5. Nothing older than 24 hours.

items.author: digitalprocessarchitect
items.title: Enterprise Agentic AI needs a roadmap
items.topicSummary: The post argues that simply giving an LLM access to tools does not make it a production-ready agent. True enterprise value from agentic AI requires a strategic roadmap that integrates business goals with technical execution.
items.warmReply: This is a critical point: agentic AI requires more than just tool access.
items.commentBody: Beyond a roadmap, the operational readiness of the business process itself is paramount. This includes defining clear exception handling, establishing robust monitoring for agent behavior, and ensuring appropriate governance frameworks are in place before scaling.
items.comment:
Warm reply: This is a critical point: agentic AI requires more than just tool access.

Beyond a roadmap, the operational readiness of the business process itself is paramount. This includes defining clear exception handling, establishing robust monitoring for agent behavior, and ensuring appropriate governance frameworks are in place before scaling.
items.whySelected: Addresses the core challenge of moving agentic AI from concept to production with a specific call for a roadmap.
items.note: My #1 recommendation today is to focus on the operational readiness of agentic AI.

items.author: lewiswalkerai
items.title: The fastest way to find high-value AI use cases
items.topicSummary: The author suggests that certain enterprise and agentic AI use cases consistently deliver value across industries. Applying these proven use cases can help organizations achieve de-risked AI adoption.
items.commentBody: Identifying high-value use cases is essential, but equally important is the design of the underlying processes to support them. A process-first redesign, rather than retrofitting AI onto existing workflows, often unlocks the most significant gains and ensures sustainable adoption.
items.comment: Identifying high-value use cases is essential, but equally important is the design of the underlying processes to support them. A process-first redesign, rather than retrofitting AI onto existing workflows, often unlocks the most significant gains and ensures sustainable adoption.
items.whySelected: Highlights practical application of AI and the importance of identifying high-value opportunities.
items.note: My #2 recommendation today is to prioritize proven AI use cases.

items.author: dilip anandan 03706329
items.title: Most companies are not struggling with AI
items.topicSummary: The post posits that the struggle for many companies isn't with AI itself, but with identifying the right solution, which could be a dashboard, better retrieval, process redesign, or an agent with controlled authority.
items.warmReply: You've hit on a key differentiator: the solution is often not just AI, but the right AI or even non-AI intervention.
items.commentBody: This perspective underscores the need for a disciplined approach to problem definition before solutioning. The 'AI' label can obscure the fundamental requirement for process optimization or improved data access, which may be the true drivers of value.
items.comment:
Warm reply: You've hit on a key differentiator: the solution is often not just AI, but the right AI or even non-AI intervention.

This perspective underscores the need for a disciplined approach to problem definition before solutioning. The 'AI' label can obscure the fundamental requirement for process optimization or improved data access, which may be the true drivers of value.
items.whySelected: Challenges the common narrative and focuses on practical problem-solving with AI as one of many tools.
items.note: My #3 recommendation today is to focus on problem definition before AI.

items.author: prashantrathi1
items.title: GenAI gets expensive long before the model
items.topicSummary: The post emphasizes that the true cost of Generative AI often lies not in the model itself, but in the infrastructure, data pipelines, and operational overhead required to deploy and manage it effectively.
items.warmReply: This is a crucial insight into the total cost of ownership for GenAI deployments.
items.commentBody: The expense often stems from the iterative nature of development and the need for robust monitoring and governance. Ensuring that pilot phases are strictly time-boxed and include clear exit criteria for moving to production can help manage these escalating costs.
items.comment:
Warm reply: This is a crucial insight into the total cost of ownership for GenAI deployments.

The expense often stems from the iterative nature of development and the need for robust monitoring and governance. Ensuring that pilot phases are strictly time-boxed and include clear exit criteria for moving to production can help manage these escalating costs.
items.whySelected: Addresses a critical, often overlooked, aspect of GenAI implementation: its true cost.
items.note: My #4 recommendation today is to manage GenAI costs proactively.

items.author: ranjanasharma
items.title: Gen AI for Cloud Solutions
items.topicSummary: The post discusses the application of Generative AI within cloud solutions, touching on concepts like RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation), AI Engineering, and LLMOps.
items.warmReply: The integration of GenAI with cloud infrastructure is fundamental to scalable deployments.
items.commentBody: Beyond RAG and LLMOps, the focus on AI Engineering highlights the need for structured development and testing. Implementing AI solutions within sprints, with defined evaluation metrics for each iteration, ensures continuous improvement and alignment with business outcomes.
items.comment:
Warm reply: The integration of GenAI with cloud infrastructure is fundamental to scalable deployments.

Beyond RAG and LLMOps, the focus on AI Engineering highlights the need for structured development and testing. Implementing AI solutions within sprints, with defined evaluation metrics for each iteration, ensures continuous improvement and alignment with business outcomes.
items.whySelected: Connects GenAI to practical engineering concerns and cloud solutions.
items.note: My #5 recommendation today is to focus on AI Engineering for GenAI.
